newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Sentiment mixed in thin talk.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Sentiment mixed in thin talk.

text.p: Sentiment in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was mixed on Thursday amid recent losses in crude values but traders said prices should be supported due to tight supplies in summer.
Talk was thin with many players staying on the sidelines, traders said.
"People should not feel bearish over the crude drops," said one trader with a U.S. trading firm.
"As we move into the summer, supplies are getting tighter. Even if cargo prices fall, they will not fall too much," the trader added.
Kuwait is reducing its exports during the summer season when its domestic need for air-conditioning rises, while some South Korean refineries are still shut or maintenance.

On the demand side, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a tender to buy at least one 38,000-tonne cargo of 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil for delivery between July 21 and August 15, a CPC official said on Thursday.
The tender, which seeks to buy low-pour fuel oil, will close on June 18 and offers will be valid for two days.
The Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organization (KEDO) has also tendered to buy 70,000 tonnes of fuel oil with maximum 2.0-percent sulphur content for July delivery to North Korea.
Bid for the tender are due June 19.
The Singapore weekly residues stocks rose by 436,000 barrels to 10.748 million barrels for the week ending June 11, Singapore's Trade Development Board (TDB) said.
The SIMEX fuel oil futures contract was still not traded on late Thursday and most traders said they were bearish about the contract.
"When the cargo market is so quiet, who wants to trade the futures market?" said one trader.
